title: Annotatio V §.I: merely spiritual vs sacramental; Sacred Supper = corporal + spiritual eating
pass_a_gloss: This is either merely spiritual, performed without union with any Corporal eating; or at the same time Sacramental, having united with it a certain Corporal Eating enjoined by GOD. Of the last kind is Eating in the Sacred Supper — inasmuch as if legitimate and such as Christ instituted, it is composed of a double eating, namely Corporal and Spiritual, and that because of the double food offered and to be received in the Sacred Supper: the one spiritual or heavenly, namely the Lord’s Body; the other corporal or earthly, bread, though by consecration extrinsically or relatively sacred, i.e. separated from common use. The Spiritual, because by itself and its nature it can be without the Sacramental, just as by accident and from the Communicant’s Impiety the Sacramental can be without the Spiritual; hence it comes about that Spiritual and Sacramental Eating stand to each other after the manner of exceeding and exceeded terms.
pass_b_english: Improper spiritual eating is either merely spiritual (no corporal union) or Sacramental (joined to a God-enjoined corporal eating).

The Sacred Supper, as Christ instituted it, is of this last kind: corporal + spiritual eating for double food — Lord’s Body (heavenly) and consecrated bread (earthly). Spiritual can stand without sacramental, and (by the unworthy) sacramental without spiritual.
source_text: Hæc vel merè spiritualis, citra unionem cum Corporali quacunque peracta; vel insimul Sacramentalis, unitam habens Manducationem quandam à DEO injunctam Corporalem. Postremi generis est Manducatio in Cœna Sacra, utpote si legitima & talis qualis à Christo instituta, ex duplici manducatione composita ea est, Corporali nempe, & Spirituali, idque ob duplicem in S. Cœna oblatum recipiendumque cibum, spiritualem alterum seu cœlestem, Corpus nempe Domini, alterum corporalem seu terrestrem, panem, quanquam ob consecrationem extrinsecè seu relativè sacrum, i. e. à communi usu separatum. Spiritualis, quia per se & suam naturam, absque Sacramentali esse potest, uti per accidens & ob Impietatem Communicantis, Sacramentalis absque Spirituali; evenit hinc, ut Spiritualis & Sacramentalis Manducatio habeant se per modum excedentium & excessorum terminorum.
notes: Merely spiritual vs sacramental; double Supper eating.
